title: Nana Patekar, Firebrand of Hindi and Marathi Cinema, Dies at 75
excerpt: The veteran actor, celebrated for Parinda, Krantiveer and Salaam Bombay, suffered a cardiac arrest at his Goa residence early Thursday; tributes pour in from Akshay Kumar, Ram Gopal Varma and others.
body:
• Veteran actor Nana Patekar, known for Parinda, Krantiveer, Ab Tak Chhappan and Mira Nair's Oscar-nominated Salaam Bombay, died of cardiac arrest at his Goa home early Thursday. He was 75.
  • He was found unconscious at his residence in Dona Paula and rushed to Manipal Hospital, where doctors attempted resuscitation for about 45 minutes. His death was declared at approximately 5:20 am, according to reports.
  • His son Malhar Patekar confirmed the death; a post-mortem is being conducted at Goa Medical College, and police were informed as part of medico-legal procedure.
  • Tributes poured in from across the industry, with Akshay Kumar calling him "completely his own" and Ram Gopal Varma mourning "the GOD of acting."

Veteran Indian actor Nana Patekar, whose ferocious dialogue delivery and towering screen presence made him one of Hindi and Marathi cinema's most distinctive performers, died early Thursday after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. He was 75.

According to reports, Patekar was found unconscious at his home in Dona Paula in the early hours of the morning and was rushed to Manipal Hospital, where a medical team administered CPR for roughly 45 minutes. Doctors were unable to revive him, and his death was declared at approximately 5:20 am on October 8. His son, Malhar Patekar, confirmed the death. Dr Shekhar Salkar, head of the oncology department at Manipal Hospital, told news agency ANI that Patekar had suffered a severe cardiac arrest. Because he was not a registered patient, the case was treated as medico-legal and a post-mortem is being conducted at Goa Medical College.

A voice like no other

Born Vishwanath Patekar in 1951, the actor known to generations simply as Nana began on the Marathi stage before making his screen debut in Gaman (1978). He broke through with Mira Nair's Oscar-nominated Salaam Bombay (1988) and went on to build a filmography defined by intensity: the brooding Parinda, the rabble-rousing Krantiveer, the tormented cop of Ab Tak Chhappan, the menace of Agni Sakshi, the devastating stage-to-screen turn in Natsamrat (2016), and late-career comic turns in Welcome and Housefull 5.

His performances won him three National Film Awards, and his trademark aggression and forceful delivery became a signature that younger audiences rediscovered through viral clips and memes. Few actors commanded both arthouse respect and mainstream adoration so completely.

"He was one of those rare actors who never needed to do too much to make you sit up and watch. That voice, that intensity, that honesty in every performance... he was completely his own."

— Akshay Kumar, actor

Industry in mourning

Tributes arrived quickly. Akshay Kumar, who worked with Patekar in Welcome and Housefull 5, wrote that he felt fortunate to have shared the screen with him. Filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma, who directed Patekar in Ab Tak Chhappan and The Attacks of 26/11, called him the "GOD of acting." Riteish Deshmukh and colleagues across the industry shared memories of the veteran.

Patekar is survived by his wife, from whom he was separated, and his son Malhar.

Why he mattered to the diaspora

For Indian immigrants of every generation, Patekar's films were staples of the living-room DVD shelf — Salaam Bombay for the art-house crowd, Krantiveer and Prahaar for those raised on nineties Hindi cinema, and his recent meme afterlife introducing him to a younger diaspora that knew the voice before the name. His death marks the passing of one of the last larger-than-life screen presences of that era.

What's next

Funeral and memorial details are expected from the family once the post-mortem formalities are complete. The industry will likely hold condolence meetings in Mumbai in the coming days.
